note: The gates below are real measurements, not a count of ticked boxes in a runbook. A checkbox measures whether somebody ticked a checkbox; these read the thing itself.

verdict_template.unassured: Nothing measurable is stopping a tag; monitoring is still landing on {unassured} of {total} checks a release has to pass, and the plans are filed.

goals.statement: We can say what the next release gives a player, and every one of those claims matches something in the build or a project building it.
goals.statement_short: we cannot say what the next release actually offers a player
goals.why_it_matters: This is the inventory. Without it Sales has nothing to take to a player, a storefront or a press contact — and the only number the wall could show was a commit count, which is how much work happened rather than what any of it gives anybody.

path_to_green.narrative: Every feature the release claims has to resolve to something in the history or to a project carrying it. One that resolves to neither is a wish on a release plan.

goals.statement: We can see what happens after somebody reaches the store page — visits, plays, and what they do next.
goals.statement_short: we cannot see anything a player does at the storefront
goals.why_it_matters: The split with Marketing: they generate demand — the posts, the press, the creators — and they own reach and interest. Sales owns everything from the store page down: who arrived, who played, who came back, who bought, who refunded and why. Wishlists sit exactly on that line, which is why they belong on both walls with different questions attached — Marketing asks whether the campaign moved the number, Sales asks what the number forecasts for launch and whether it clears the visibility bar the storefront uses. None of it is visible here: one free browser build has been live for weeks and nobody in this studio can say whether a single person has opened it.

path_to_green.narrative: One credential. The storefront already counts views and plays for us; we have simply never asked it for the numbers. That is the only view of demand this studio has today, and it is the cheapest real thing on my list.

goals.statement: The credits screen exists and opens — the attribution we owe actually ships.
goals.statement_short: the credits screen the licence depends on is not wired up
goals.why_it_matters: One shipped asset is attribution-required. If the screen carrying that attribution does not open in the build, the release is not licence-clean, whatever the ledger says.

measure.label: a credits screen is wired into the title menu
measure.says_false: no credits screen is wired into the title menu

path_to_green.narrative: Wire the credits screen before the tag.

escalates.because: The attribution is owed to the person whose work we shipped, and it is owed the moment the build is public — not when we get round to the screen.

goals.statement: Somebody played the actual web build end to end before it went out.
goals.statement_short: nothing records that the web build was played before a tag
goals.why_it_matters: The runbook's first line, and the one nothing can automate: sound has to arrive after the first tap, and only a person in a browser can tell you it did. So it is recorded rather than measured — your yes, against the tag being cut and the commit the build came from. It is spent when that tag goes out, and it lapses early if the game changes after you played it.

path_to_green.narrative: Ten minutes in a browser on the build the next tag would ship, then the button on this row.

goals.statement: Every storefront we are live on, we can still publish to.
goals.statement_short: we are live on a storefront we can no longer publish to
goals.unit: live storefronts we cannot publish to
goals.why_it_matters: A channel we cannot push to is worse than one we are not on: it looks like a way to reach players and is not. The pipeline, the preset and the credential behind each live storefront are verified rather than assumed.

path_to_green.narrative: Open the ladder below and fix whatever the live storefront is missing.

escalates.because: Players can reach this storefront today, and a channel we cannot publish to leaves whatever is on it standing.
